summary: Sravani Kanamarlapudi is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. She studied as a PhD student at the University of Texas at Austin around 2018 under Richard G. Salomon and studied at the University of Washington in 2019.

Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Visva-Bharati University, Andhra University, and the University of Marburg (PhD circa 1963–1966), later serving as a professor at Aligarh Muslim University from around 1977 to 1997.

Sri Anirvan (1896–1978) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed his studies at the University of Dhaka around 1910–1912, Sanskrit College and University around 1912–1916, and the University of Calcutta around 1916–1918.

Sri Aurobindo (1872–1950) was a scholar in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at King's College, Cambridge, and under Robert Mason Towers, Dinendra Kumar Ray, and Vishnu Bhaskar Lele, later holding a post at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (circa 1893–1906).

Srikanth Kaul worked in Indology and history/archaeology. In 1967, he was attested as a professor at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir, and held an attested post at Government Degree College, Sopore.

Srimanta Bhadra works in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He earned a PhD from Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda Educational and Research Institute by 2021 and became an assistant professor at Raja Narendra Lal Khan Women's College in 2017.

Srinivas H. Ritti (1928–2021) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He served as an epigraphical assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India (1964) and Government Epigraphist for India (1965), and as professor at Karnatak University (1975).

Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan (1932–2019) was an Indology scholar who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Hamburg around 1960–1967. He subsequently served as Privatdozent für Indologie at the University of Hamburg from 1973 to 1997.

Srinivasa Kumar N Acharya works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Poornaprajna Vidyapeetha, earning an MA Vidvat-uttama Navya-nyaya, and became an assistant professor at Manipal Academy of Higher Education in 2011.

Sriram Krishnan works in computational fields, Indology, and linguistics. He has held posts at Central Sanskrit University, the International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad, and the University of Hyderabad.

Sriram Subramanian works in Indology and computational fields. He studied at Pondicherry Engineering College, University of Cincinnati, Hindu University of America (PhD 2019), and MIT Group of Institutions, later becoming a principal software engineer at Microsoft in 2022.

Srisa Chandra Vasu (1861–1918) was an Indologist and philosopher educated at Government College University, Lahore. He served as a vakil at Allahabad High Court around 1883, founded the Panini Office in 1891, and became a fellow at the University of Allahabad around 1899.

Stacey Boulter works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She studied at Dalhousie University (BA 2016–2025) and McMaster University (MA 2025), where she also held a post as a teaching assistant in 2025.

Stacey Van Vleet is a scholar of Tibetology, history/archaeology, and Sinology. She studied at the University of Colorado Boulder and Columbia University (PhD attested 2006) under Carole McGranahan and Tashi Tsering Josayma, and held a post at Columbia attested in 2013.

Stamford Raffles (1781–1826) worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He held posts with the East India Company, served as Chief Secretary of Prince of Wales Island (1807), was Governor of Java (circa 1811–1816), and became president of the Zoological Society of London in 1826.

Stanford E. Lehmberg (1931–2012) was a history and archaeology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Christopher Morris around 1954–1956 and later served at the University of Minnesota from around 1969 to 1999.

Stanislao Gatti (1820–1870) was a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He studied at the University of Naples Federico II from around 1836 to 1840 and later held a post there from around 1861 until 1870.

Stanislas Guyard (1846–1884) was an Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics scholar. He served at the École Pratique des Hautes Études starting in 1868 and became professor of Arabic at the Collège de France in 1884.

Stanislas Julien (1797–1873) was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat. He held chairs of Greek (1821) and Chinese (1832–1873) at the Collège de France and taught at INALCO (1862–1871).

Stanislav Grof is a scholar who studied at Charles University (circa 1951–1956). His career included posts at Johns Hopkins University (1967–1969), the Maryland Psychiatric Research Center (1969–1973), Esalen Institute (1973–1987), and the California Institute of Integral Studies (1994–2015).
